item.title: Docker on Raspberrypi
item.description:
After a lot of trial and error, including reinstalling Pi OS Lite, multiple times, here is how I succesfully installed Docker and Miniflux (RSS feed).

I’m using a RaspberryPi 5, I’ve just installed a fresh version of Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit), and I’ve updated and upgraded.

Docker

  1. Install docker
curl -sSL https://get.docker.com | sh
  1. Add your user to the docker group (to properly interact with docker)
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

Then reboot and thereafter check if you successfully added yourself to the docker group with the groups command. If docker is mentioned in the output, you did it successfully and should now be ready to use docker.

item.title: Syncthing on Linux
item.description:
This is a page about »Syncthing on Linux«.

Debian/RaspberryPi (Years ago, probably outdated)

Follow the documentation

Then nano ~/.config/syncthing/config.xml

Find the following

<gui enabled="true" tls="false" debugging="false">
<address>127.0.0.1:8384</address>
<apikey></apikey>
<theme>default</theme>
</gui>

And replace the 127.0.0.1:8384 with 0.0.0.0:8384. Now any machine on the local network can access the program.
Save and Close

Fedora

sudo dnf in syncthing

Make it start on system boot.

To make it a service that can start up on it’s own when turning on the machine
systemctl enable syncthing@[username].service
systemctl start syncthing@[username].service to start it right away
Make sure to replace [username] with your username.

item.title: How to Stay Safe Browsing the Web
item.description:
This is a page about »How to stay safe while browsing the Web«.

Starting out with this post lacking a few things. I will update it later where I also include links to the things I’m talking about.

  1. Install an adblocker on your browser (This can be tricky if you use google chrome, and I highly recommend using another browser.)

Why install an adblocker?

I have experienced so many times where I’ve told a friend or family member to download a program from a website I’ve specified. They click download on the website I’ve specified, and to my surprise they didn’t download the correct thing. The reason being, I use an adblocker but they didn’t and the ads they see say “download”. This clearly shows that ads are a huge security nightmare. There’s also so many other annoyances ads include, sponsored search results (ads) can be leading you to a website containing malware, they can play unwanted sound and the list goes on. So really, I very much recommend you to Install an adblocker.

item.title: Windows - First Steps
item.description:
Here’s what I do when I’ve just installed windows on my or a friends computer.

  1. Go to Microsoft Store and make sure things in there is updated.

  2. Run Chris Titus Tech’s Windows Utility (Github link).
    Here I will:

  • Set the computer to delay feature updates for Windows. Security updates will still be installed, but the updates that bring new features that isn’t needed will be delayed.
  • Activate “Set Up Autologin” for some friends. (Config tab).
  • Disable Search Box Web Suggestions.
  • Go to the Tweaks tab, press Standard, and go through what it does. In this tool you can point with your mouse on differing things and it will give you more information about what that thing does.
  • Change DNS in a lot of cases, but not on my own PCs as I’m running Pi.Hole on my network.
  • Run OO Shutup 10, to prevent Windows from spying.
  • Create Winutil shortcut and Run tweaks. Winutil can also be used to install software.

  1. Install a browser through the command prompt (CMD) using Winget. To install firefox winget install Mozilla.Firefox To install brave winget install Brave.Brave Then I will also go to Settings > Apps > Default Apps in Windows and pick the installed browser as default browser.
